押.story: Use your fingers (扌) to make sure the roots (甲) of your plant are deep underground by pushing them down, down, down.
押.readings: オウ / お.す・お.し-・お.っ-

抽.story: If you pluck your fingers (扌), new ones will sprout (由) in their place. (try it ;).

担.story: One of Hercules' labors was to hold the world in his fingers (扌) for Atlas and not move until sunrise (旦), shouldering the considerable burden.
担.readings: タン / かつ.ぐ・にな.う

拉.story: I crush my fingers (扌) trying to lift a heavy vase (立).
拉.readings: ラツ・ラ・ロウ / らっ.する・ひし.ぐ・くだ.く

拍.story: Image: the most snooty prim and proper English Lord with white (白) gloves clapping only with his fingers (扌). "Oh bravo old chap. Bravo..."

拐.story: Wrap your fingers (扌) around someone's mouth (口) to keep them quiet, then put the dagger (刀) to their throat to ensure their cooperation. This is the best way to kidnap someone.

拒.story: What's the rudest way to refuse a proposal? Well lifting the finger (扌) that is gigantic (巨), the middle finger (扌) of course! Think of Neo refusing Agent Smith's proposal in the Matrix if it helps: "How about I give you the finger (扌)?"

拓.story: A huge index finger (扌) coming down from the sky is kicking stones (石), to clear the land. Maybe it's the finger (扌) of God preparing a place for his little people to live.

拘.story: You approach the thief from behind, stick two fingers (扌) at his back to fake a gun, and say the phrase (句) "You're under arrest".

拙.story: With fingers (扌) fumbling around trying to get the key in the door so he could exit (出), the clumsy husband woke his wife as he tried to leave for a rendezvous with his mistress.

招.story:
A Geisha beckons you with her index finger (扌), and as you approach she runs her fingers (扌) all over her body in an attempt to summon (召) you into her chambers. Keyword meaning : “invite”.
This is NOT kidnap (拐)

拝.story: People are putting their hands (扌) together and worshipping the bush (丰) hanging from the ceiling (一) because it has the shape of Virgin Mary.
拝.readings: ハイ / おが.む・おろが.む

拠.story: When rockclimbing, when your weight disposes (処) of the valuable foothold, all that's left is your fingers (扌) keeping you from death. Meanwhile, your walking legs (夂) are left dangling in the wind (几).

拡.story: Spread your fingers (扌) wide (広) to broaden your hand.
拡.readings: カク・コウ / ひろ.がる・ひろ.げる・ひろ.める

括.story: Teacher was always telling us to fasten our lips by pulling a zipper shut with our fingers (扌). It always frightened me because I imagined getting my tongue (舌) stuck in the zipper.

拭.story: Why carry a handkerchief? I wipe my nose finger(扌)-style(式).
拭.readings: ショク・シキ / ぬぐ.う・ふ.く

拳.story: I hold a roll of quarters (龹) in my hand (手) when I make a fist.
拳.readings: ケン・ゲン / こぶし

拶.story: The old lady said that there was a flood (巛) imminent, because her fingers (扌) hurt in the evening (夕).

拷.story: In Torture 101 class they teach you to consider (考) the fingers (扌) as the first part to inflict pain to. Then you can move on to other parts.

拾.story: I tried to pick up the bowling ball...but my fingers (扌) didn't fit (合) in the holes.
拾.readings: シュウ・ジュウ / ひろ.う

持.story: In the Buddhist temple (寺) monks develop insane finger (扌) strength and are trained to hold positions for ridiculously long periods of time.
持.readings: ジ / も.つ・-も.ち・も.てる

指.readings: シ / ゆび・さ.す・-さ.し

挑.story: The rabbit pointed his finger (扌) at the turtle (兆) and said, "I challenge you for a race!" The rest is history...

挙.story: One of my main entertainments (兴=興) has been the design of a special owl(⺍)-luring tool (具). All you need is to raise it in your hand (手). Owl (⺍) will come flying and perch on it right away.
挙.readings: キョ / あ.げる・あ.がる・こぞ.る

挟.story: You know how in Tokyo there are those really packed trains where train staff in gloves shove people in? Well imagine being sandwiched in so tight, that when the doors close, only your fingers (扌) are sticking out, and they get caught between the doors, not letting them fully close. The train staff have no choice, they must cut them off with scissors (夹).
挟.readings: キョウ・ショウ / はさ.む・はさ.まる・わきばさ.む

挨.story: Like arrows (矢), the whole family was exchanging elbows (厶) and hands (扌) during the greeting at the bicentennial family gathering. There was no need to use any sentence particles (矣) during our greeting.

挫.story: I sprained my fingers (扌) when I sat in meditation (坐) (by sitting in a strange position).
挫.readings: ザ・サ / くじ.く・くじ.ける

振.story: Bruce Lee (辰) only needs his pinky finger (扌) to swing his babies asleep.
振.readings: シン / ふ.る・ふ.れる・ふ.るう

挿.story: A rice farmer's delicate fingers (扌) have inserted 1,000 (千) rooted (甲) seedlings into his field.
挿.readings: ソウ / さ.す・はさ.む

捉.story:
Leon S. Kennedy thought he had escaped the zombies, when suddenly he felt a hand (扌) nabbing his foot (足). It was still alive.
nab: to catch or seize in arrest, to seize suddenly.
捉.readings: ソク・サク / とら.える

捕.story: Offspring (甫) are pretty slippery when they come out of the womb; be sure to catch the baby with your fingers (扌) so it doesn't slide and fall on the floor!
捕.readings: ホ / と.らえる・と.らわれる・と.る

捗.story: "Come on people, the only way to make headway in this business is to let your fingers (扌) do the walking (歩)! bust out the yellow pages and dial as many numbers as possible, surely someone is a sucker for a cold call sell."
捗.readings: チョク・ホ / はかど.る

捜.story: Heard about the fourth wise monkey (申)? Often overlooked after Hear, See and Speak no Evil, he's Searches no Evil. Picture the four famous monkeys at Nikko, the fourth covering his crotch (又) with his fingers (扌), showing he won't be searching for any evil deeds in that evil place.
捜.readings: ソウ・シュ・シュウ / さが.す

捨.story: Someone stuck their fingers (扌) in my cottage (舎) cheese! I'm going to have to discard the lot!

据.story: The man set (in position) his finger (扌) firmly on the map and said "Here is where they reside (居), I am certain of it".
据.readings: キョ / す.える・す.わる

捻.story:
Ever try wrenching a bolt with just your fingers (扌)? Trust me, you'll wish (念) you had a wrench for wrenching to save your fingers (扌) from the pain.
wrench: to pull or tighten by violent twisting or with violence. to move with a violent twist. to twist, to turn (a switch on or off, etc.).
捻.readings: ネン・ジョウ / ね.じる・ねじ.る・ひね.くる

掃.story: Whether I sweep something away with my fingers (扌) or my broom (彐), I should always wear my apron (帚).

授.story: "Please accept (受) this finger (扌)" you say, imparting it to your yakuza boss.
授.readings: ジュ / さず.ける・さず.かる

掌.story: Instead of magazines, we keep a Rubiks Cube in the outhouse (尚) to manipulate with your hands (手) while you do your business.
掌.readings: ショウ / てのひら・たなごころ

排.story: I gave the principal the finger (扌) so they expelled me from school and sent me to jail (非) in the janitor's closet.

掘.story: If you dig with your fingers (扌) hard enough, soil eventually yields (屈).

掛.story: 4 ways you could hang something: 1) the normal way, with your finger (扌) putting something on a hook or whatever, 2) hanging from a vine (圭) the natural way, 3) by means of the magic wand (卜) or 4) through a divination sign (卦).
掛.readings: カイ・ケイ / か.ける・-か.ける・か.け

採.story: He pointed his finger (扌) at the vulture (爫) sitting in the tree (木) playing dice (采) and said, "I think I can pick him off from here."

探.story: When Miss World (㓁) climbed on top of that tree (木) she left her crown (冖) on top of it, and now she's groping for it with her fingers (扌) inside the tiny hole (罙) that squirrels usually dig in trees.
探.readings: タン / さぐ.る・さが.す

接.story:
A pervert meets a woman (女). The pervert tries to come in contact with his lustful fingers (扌). The woman (女) takes a vase (立), lifts it over her head and smashes it on the pervert's head. Later on she becomes my concubine (妾).
concubine: a woman who lives with a man but has lower status than his wife or wives.
Kiss/kissing (接吻) = contact (接) + proboscis (吻)
接.readings: セツ・ショウ / つ.ぐ

控.story: My hands (扌) were empty (空), so I had to withhold myself from fighting the 空手[から.て] master, because, although his hands (手) were empty (空) as well, he seemed to always be in waiting for a good combat.
控.readings: コウ / ひか.える・ひか.え

推.story:
In the midst of conjecture on whether it was done or not, mom stuck her fingers (扌) in the turkey (隹) to check.
conjecture: an opinion or conclusion formed on the basis of incomplete information.

措.story: Once upon a time (昔) our ancestors set aside the use of fingers (扌) and began to use cutlery.

掲.story: A muchacho (匂) puts up a notice that says “NO FINGER SNAPPING ALLOWED. MUCHACHOS (匂) ON SIESTA (曷)”. The muchachos are sleeping soundly, completely oblivious to the sound of dogs barking, guitar playing and even gun shots. Now imagine one tourist passing by and snapping his fingers (扌) and waking up all the muchachos (匂) at once from the siesta (曷).

掻.story: Insects (虫) on your crotch (又) make your fingers (扌) want to scratch. Scratching with your fingers (扌) is a possible sign of a flea (蚤) infestation. Even when they are gone, the urge to scratch remains.

描.story: Isn't finger (扌) paint great? This kanji shows a kid finger (扌) painting a sketch of a flowery (艹) field (田).
描.readings: ビョウ / えが.く・か.く

提.story: You raise your finger (扌) at a meeting, to propose things to be done with justice (是).
提.readings: テイ・チョウ・ダイ / さ.げる

揚.story: My piggy bank (昜) is so heavy that I cannot hoist it using just my fingers (扌).
揚.readings: ヨウ / あ.げる・-あ.げ・あ.がる

換.story: After months of practice, you finally managed to teach a nice trick to your sled-pulling four (四) bound up (⺈) St. Bernard dogs (大): one snap of your fingers (扌) and they interchange their positions.
換.readings: カン / か.える・-か.える・か.わる

握.story: Fingers (扌) gripping the rooftop (屋) as you're about to fall to your death.

揮.story:
An army (軍) leader in his chariot (車) is brandishing his finger (扌) at the enemy, crying "chaaaaaaaaarrrgggeeee!"
brandish: wave or flourish (something, especially a weapon) as a threat or in anger or excitement.

援.story:
You abet the escape of migrating ducks (爰) by pointing them the way with your finger (扌).
abet: encourage or assist (someone) to do something wrong, in particular, to commit a crime or other offense.

揺.story: A condor (䍃) is a vulture (爫) who lives in very arid and dry (干) mountains (山). Once it takes a hold of a prey, with its finger(扌)-like claws (爫), it shakes them until they die.
揺.readings: ヨウ / ゆ.れる・ゆ.る・ゆ.らぐ

損.story: Boss yells, "Who damaged the Xerox machine?!" fingers (扌) of employees (員) point at one another.
損.readings: ソン / そこ.なう・そこな.う・-そこ.なう

搬.story: When workers neglect workplace safety, their fingers (扌) get cut off and carried away by the conveyor belt, which looks like a 'finger (扌) carrier (般)' in that case.

搭.story: When you board a plane to Hawaii, a crew-member takes a hand(扌)-made flower (艹) lei and fits (合) it around your neck.

携.story: Because they have no fingers (扌), turkeys (隹) must use their fists (乃)when dialing on a portable phone.
携.readings: ケイ / たずさ.える・たずさ.わる

搾.story: Very simple visual image makes this an easy kanji to remember. Just picture that you squeeze your fingers (扌) going through the tight (窄) hole (穴) in the handle of the saw (乍). You then squeeze your fingers (扌) tight to use the saw (乍) to cut a tight (窄) hole (穴).

摂.story: One way to intake some nutrients is to take your finger (扌), dig around in your ear (耳), then eat whatever sparkling (＊) matter you may find.
摂.readings: セツ・ショウ / おさ.める・かね.る・と.る

摘.story: My grandma always pinched me with her fingers (扌) when I was playing with her antiques (啇). Imagine her fingers (扌), also quite antique (啇), thin, bony and hard, pinching at your hand (扌). "Keep your fingers (扌) away from my antiques (啇)!!".

摩.story: If you grind the hemp (麻) without a stone but use your hand (手) instead it will chafe. (Image: "Robin, why are your hands all chafed?" 'Uh... (I've been grinding hemp all day)').
摩.readings: マ / ま.する・さす.る・す.る

摯.story:
The earnest look out for others: when you fall over, they’ll grab your hand (手 ) with tenacity (執) and pull you back up.
earnest: resulting from or showing sincere and intense conviction. sincere.
摯.readings: シ / いた.る・つか.む・にえ

撃.story: Your car (車) has missiles (殳)?! That beats mine, hands (手) down.

撤.story: The taskmaster (攵) brings up (育) his infant (ㄊ) so that whenever he doesn't wash his hands (扌) before eating, there is a withdrawal of video games and TV priviledges.

撮.story: Take (取) the utmost (最) care that you don't have your finger (扌) in the way when you take a snapshot.
撮.readings: サツ / と.る・つま.む・-ど.り

撲.story: My husband (夫) has been proposing that in 相撲(すもう) wrestling, instead of them using their hands (扌) to slap each other out of the ring, fighters should be wearing viking horned helmets (丵) and charge at each other. We can also hire fat viking husbands (菐) to fight.

擁.story: A mysterious (玄) turkey (隹) with human fingers (扌) wants to hug me... I will never go to Tokyo Disneyland again!

操.story: Luke Skywalker points his fingers (扌) and uses the force to maneuver the goods (品) through the tree (木) branches and up over the tree (木) while the chirping of birds (喿) is heard in the background.
操.readings: ソウ・サン / みさお・あやつ.る

擦.story: If you mis-guess (察) the cheese you'll scrape your fingers (扌) on the cheese-grater (happens to me all the time).
擦.readings: サツ / す.る・す.れる・-ず.れ

擬.story: Ask a mime to mimic doubt (疑), and he will no doubt (疑) scratch his head with his finger (扌).
擬.readings: ギ / まが.い・もど.き

支.story: With ten (十) good right hands (又), my men can provide the support that you need.
支.readings: シ / ささ.える・つか.える・か.う

改.story: This is a Meiji reformation taskmaster (攵), trying to force usage of the Roman alphabet in Japan in place of Kanji. He holds a snake (已) in the shape of the letter S and tries to explain how much simpler this is
改.readings: カイ / あらた.める・あらた.まる

攻.story: The special craft (工) of successful taskmasters (攵) is their ability to remain constantly on the aggressive, never allowing their underlings a moment to ponder a counter-aggression of their own.

放.story: Go in any direction (方) away from your taskmaster (攵) when you are set free.
放.readings: ホウ / はな.す・-っぱな.し・はな.つ

政.story: Those involved in politics are always trying to elect the correct (正) taskmaster (攵).
政.readings: セイ・ショウ / まつりごと・まん

故.story: An old (古) taskmaster (攵) who has managed to win the election by happenstance/coincidence.
故.readings: コ / ゆえ・ふる.い・もと

敏.story: Cleverness is something every (毎) taskmaster (攵) must have. Every (毎) taskmaster (攵) has cleverness.

救.story: For salvation you have to request (求) forgiveness from God, the ultimate taskmaster (攵).

敗.story: The shellfish (貝) who was defeated (負) before is being chastised by the taskmaster ( 攵) for his failure to win.

教.story: In early Japan, filial piety (孝) was the cornerstone of education, and harsh taskmaster (攵) were employed to teach it.
教.readings: キョウ / おし.える・おそ.わる

敢.story: Only a truly daring Japanese student would put a spike (丅) through his ear (耳) under the gaze of the Japanese teacher taskmasters (攵)!
敢.readings: カン / あ.えて・あ.えない・あ.えず

散.story: The taskmaster (攵) is dissatisfied with the meal she's served, and scatters the salad (龷) and the meat (月) across the floor for the servants to clean up.
散.readings: サン / ち.る・ち.らす・-ち.らす

敬.story: In order to show awe and honor to your taskmaster (攵), use phrases (句) filled with flowers (艹), praise, and honor, in other words, use 敬語(けい.ご).
敬.readings: ケイ・キョウ / うやま.う

数.story: The taskmaster (攵) makes you count the number of stars in the constellation (娄).
数.readings: スウ・ス・サク / かず・かぞ.える・しばしば

整.story: Recycling in Japan, you have to make sure all your bundles (束) are organized correctly (正) otherwise the taskmasters (攵) won't accept them.
整.readings: セイ / ととの.える・ととの.う

敵.story: The taskmaster (攵) became my enemy for life when he smashed the antique (啇) vase holding my wife's ashes.
敵.readings: テキ / かたき・あだ・かな.う

敷.story: The acupunturist (尃) decided to spread his attention in many directions (方), and be a taskmaster (攵) at none. He announced (旉) it to his boss and he wasn't so happy about it.

文.story: Under the familiar top hat (亠) we see a crisscross (乂) pattern or design, like that found on woodwork or garments. This should make an ugly enough image to help remember it. It can be associated with sentence by thinking of a sentence as a grammatical pattern.
文.readings: ブン・モン / ふみ・あや

斉.story: The two (二) between the fenceposts (丌) is similar to the mathematical equal sign. The recruits in the boot camp have to train physically with fenceposts (丌), without uttering any sentenes (文). They all have to wear equal uniforms and sing in unison (斉唱) in the choir (齐) when required. They are all of equal value in the infantry.
斉.readings: セイ・サイ / そろ.う・ひと.しい・ひと.しく

斎.story: As the chorus (齐) sings, an exorcism, or "purification" of the soul is taking place. The possessed girl is tied to two fenceposts (丌) to the sides of the altar (示), her head spinning around and around. Then the priest says the required sentence (文): "The power of Christ compels you!"
斎.readings: サイ / とき・つつし.む・ものいみ

斑.story:
The sentences (文) exchanged between the two kings (王) got more and more heated, finally leading to a fight which left the whole area speckled with blood.
speckled: covered or marked with a large number of small spots or patches of color.

斗.story: The Big Dipper here is of course the constellation of Ursa Major, of which this kanji is a sort of pictographic representation. The Big Dipper is a celestial measuring cup (斗).

料.story: When buying rice (米), the fee is calculated by the cup. Naturally we don't just use any cup; it has to be a proper measuring cup (斗).

斜.story: The scale (余) tilts diagonally when a measuring cup (斗) filled with too much (余) is set on one end.
斜.readings: シャ / なな.め・はす

斤.story: The axe-wielding maniac drags (⺁) his latest victim to nail (丅) them to their basement.

斥.story: The kids at school used to reject me.. Made me feel really bad till I brought my axe (斤) to school. See the drop (丶) of blood on it?

斬.story: I wanted a convertible so I chopped off the top of my car (車) with an axe (斤).
斬.readings: ザン・サン・セン / き.る

断.story: After he got hooked (乚) on rice (米) wine the Japanese salaryman got the axe (斤) at work. Now all he has to live on is serverance pay.
断.readings: ダン / た.つ・ことわ.る・さだ.める

新.story: The Red Hot Chili Peppers (亲) and Axe(斤)l Rose form a new band.
新.readings: シン / あたら.しい・あら.た・あら-

方.story:
I always keep my directions bound (勹) to the bottom of my top hat (亠) so I won't lose them.
仕方がない(し.かた.がない)[it can't be helped; it's inevitable]
方.readings: ホウ / かた・-かた・-がた

施.story: Under their banner (方乛), volunteers are requesting alms/donations for scorpion (也) sting victims.

旅.story: After a long long trip, what once was a proud beautiful banner (方乛), we had nothing more than a simple rag (衣) remaining.

旋.story: A merry-go-round with a big banner (方乛) on top and below a veritable zoo (疋) of bakelite animals on poles in perpertual rotation accompanied by silly music. Giraffes, elephants, zebras, rhinos…
旋.readings: セン / め.ぐる・いばり

族.story: With a banner (方乛) declaring "Keep Out!" and throwing arrows (矢) to back it up, the Amazon tribe is not that friendly.

旗.story: The United Republic of Chess' national flag is actually a banner (方乛) with a rook (其), that way they can hang it at every tournament.

既.story: There is no need to get cash for the tip, we have already left some silver (艮) on the table for the waitress (旡).

日.readings: ニチ・ジツ / ひ・-び・-か

旦.story: The sun (日) rising over one (一) horizon signifies the sunrise.
旦.readings: タン・ダン / あき.らか・あきら・ただし

旧.story: In olden times, gentlemen used walking sticks (丨) every day (日).
旧.readings: キュウ / ふる.い・もと

旨.story: Something is so downright delicious that one spends the entire day (日) with a spoon (匕) in hand gobbling it up.

早.story: The sun (日) up is early, well before ten (十).
早.readings: ソウ・サッ / はや.い・はや・はや-

旬.story: Japan wraps up (勹) the days (日) of the month into three 10-day periods (しゅん). The first is 上旬 (じょうじゅん); the second is 中旬 (ちゅうじゅん); the last is 下旬 (げじゅん).

旭.story: Baseball (九) under the sun (日) is popular in Japan, the land of the rising sun.

旺.story: After the sun (日) shone through his window, the king (王) became once more vigorous, and ready to rule.

昆.story: A grandfather watches his descendants playing outside under the sun (日), silently comparing (比) them, considering which of them will grow up and make him proud. Suddenly, grandma calls them in for a snack of 昆布(kombu) and for a re-application of repellent to keep the 昆虫(insects) away.

昇.story: You know that you got a promotion when your measuring box (升) has enough dollar bills in it to reach the sun (日).

昌.story: If you work from sun (日) up to sun (日) down you will be prosperous.

明.story: The sun (日) makes the moon (月) bright.
明.readings: メイ・ミョウ・ミン / あ.かり・あか.るい・あか.るむ

昏.story: At dusk every day I go out in one of those airplanes that leaves a vapour trail and write my family name (氏) just above the setting sun (日). I have to wait until dusk so that the sun (日) is low enough in the sky.
昏.readings: コン / くら.い・くれ

易.story: The sun (日) is not (勿) an easy place to get to.
易.readings: エキ・イ / やさ.しい・やす.い

昔.story:
Once upon a time I was in my salad (龷) days (日), when I was green in judgment, cold in blood...
one's salad days: expression meaning a youthful time, accompanied by the inexperience, enthusiasm, idealism, innocence, or indiscretion that one associates with a young person.
昔.readings: セキ・シャク / むかし

星.story:
The sun (日) is the nearest star to the only planet with life (生) - Earth.
聖闘士星矢[セイ.トウ.{シ}.セイ.や](saint.fight.warrior.star.arrow)Saint Seiya
星.readings: セイ・ショウ / ほし・-ぼし

映.story: In the solar system, the sun (日) is the central (央) source of all light, everything else just reflects it.
映.readings: エイ / うつ.る・うつ.す・は.える

髭.story: "Please stop (止) and sit down (匕) to look to this here (此) painting", the tour guide says. "We don't know exactly who is on the painting, but from the shape (彡) of the hair (镸) and the distinctive moustache, we think they meant to depict President Theodore Roosevelt."
髭.readings: シ / ひげ・くちひげ

鬱.story: In the middle of the gloomy grove (林) you find a tin can (缶), containing a beautiful crown (冖), and a flask with very nice-smelling fragrant herbs (鬯)! You feel so happy and lucky after finding these interesting items... but suddenly, they start changing shape (彡) in your hands... and turn into ashes! So, in similar fashion, your feelings, and the shape (彡) of your face, go from happy to really gloomy, and now you truly understand why this place is called the gloomy grove (林).
鬱.readings: ウツ / うっ.する・ふさ.ぐ・しげ.る

鬼.story: An oni has a single horn sticking out of its head (甶) and carries a huge club in the crook of its elbow (厶). It wanders on its human legs (儿), searching for skulls to smash open and brains (田) to devour.

魂.story:
When you die, your soul either goes to the rising clouds (云) of heaven or to be devoured by an oni (鬼) in hell.
魂のルフラン (たましいのルフラン)[Soul's Refrain]
魂.readings: コン / たましい・たま

魅.story:
The only people who have a fascination with oni (鬼) are those that have not yet (未) met one.
DAN DAN 心魅かれてく [こころ.ひかれてく](Bit By Bit I'm Falling Under Your Spell)

魔.story: Caves (广), abandoned groves (林), and onis (鬼) are often associated with demons. So is the use of drugs, like hemp (麻).

魚.story: That fish was caught, bound up (⺈), then carried across rice fields (田), and finally cooked over a fire (灬).
魚.readings: ギョ / うお・さかな・-ざかな

鮨.story: Japanese consider fish (魚) to be most delicious (旨) when eaten as sushi. (Note: In practice, sushi is more often written 寿司, but occasionally 鮨).

鮮.story: 2 examples of foods that should be purchased fresh. To remember which foods, take the first letter of fresh, "F", to stand for fish (魚) and the final sound of fresh, "SH", to stand for sheep (羊): FreSH.

鯉.story: The pond full of fish (魚) right next to my parent's home (里) is full of こい carp.

鯨.story: If fish (魚) were cities, the whale would surely be the capital (京).

鱗.story: Little known fact: Tom Cruise (粦), one of the most famous Americans (米) with sunglasses (舛) turns into a merman at night, with scales like a fish (魚) and everything. Weird.
鱗.readings: リン / うろこ・こけ・こけら

鳥.story:
A white (白) bird with one (一) massive tail feather (刁).
一石二鳥 (いっ.せき.に.ちょう)[killing two birds with one stone]

鳩.story: Pigeons are the birds (鳥) that come in hordes after baseball (九) games to eat all the trash left by fans.
鳩.readings: キュウ・ク / はと・あつ.める

鳴.story: A chirp is the sound that comes from the mouth (口) of birds (鳥).
鳴.readings: メイ / な.く・な.る・な.らす

鶏.story: "My husband (夫) is like a vulture (爫) when it comes to chicken. As soon as I begin cooking it, he's on the boundaries of my kitchen - sniffing and eyeing away, like a bird (鳥) stalking its prey."
鶏.readings: ケイ / にわとり・とり

鶴.story:
The original version of the "Ugly Duckling" was about a crane who grew up in a turkey house (隺). All the other birds (鳥) made fun of it for not having a wattle or a snood or fanning its tail.
A wattle is a fleshy caruncle hanging from various parts of the head or neck in several groups of birds and mammals.
In anatomical terms, the snood is an erectile, fleshy protuberance on the forehead of turkeys.

鹿.story: Drawn on the walls of a complex of caves (广) near Niaux in southern France are a number of animal likenesses dating from the Upper Paleolithic period. Among them we find pictures of deer, some of them showing men in deermasks. By comparing (比) their drawings to real deer, Stone Age people hoped to acquire power over the animal in the hunt; and by comparing (比) themselves to the deer, to take on that animal's characteristics. But time has locked with a "double-key" (龷 + |) the real secret of this art form from us, and we can only surmise such meanings. But more important than the enigmas of the troglodytic mind is the way in which caves (广), a double-key (龷 + |), and comparing (比) gives us the kanji for deer.

麒.story:
A deer (鹿)with a rook(其)-shaped neck probably is a giraffe.
麒麟 = Giraffe.

麓.story: Many deer (鹿) can be found in the grove (林) at the foot of a mountain.

麗.story: Even if Li (丽) Yang was a deer (鹿), she would still look lovely.
麗.readings: レイ / うるわ.しい・うら.らか

麟.story:
As a Scientologist, a deer (鹿) to Tom Cruise (粦) is not just a deer (鹿). It is actually a descendent of a camelopard that was sent by extraterrestrials.
麒麟 = Giraffe.

麦.story: Barley is a very cheap grain, and it's not really worth spending time to harvest. Therefore, scientists have genetically engineered it to grow walking legs (夂) once the grain is grown up (龶) and mature, so it can harvest itself.

麺.story: I always eat barley (麦) noodles with a mask (面) on - it stops them splashing in your face.
麺.readings: メン・ベン / むぎこ

麻.story: The world's most prolific drug dealer maintains a massive grove (林) of hemp in a cave (广) to avoid law enforcement.

黄.story: My face turned yellow when I watched my salad (龷) sprout (由) animal legs (ハ) and start scurrying across the table. Check please!
黄.readings: コウ・オウ / き・こ-

黒.story: If your parent's home (里) catches on fire (灬), it will turn black.
黒.readings: コク / くろ・くろ.ずむ・くろ.い

黙.story: The computer (里) won't stop beeping, which is making the dog (犬) bark, and it's driving this guy insane. The only solution he can come up with is to throw them both on the fire (灬) and finally enjoy the silence.
黙.readings: モク・ボク / だま.る・もだ.す

鼓.story: The samurai (士) wanted to buy a drum, but at his local music store, the salesman said, "Frankly, the drums we have here aren't worth beans (豆). You'd do better at one of our store's other branches (支)."

鼻.story: I blew my nose (自) so hard my brain (田) came out in my two hands (廾).

齢.story: Your teeth (歯) have a lot to do with your age;/When you have none, you're infant or sage;/Once you grow teeth, you leave your home's borders/And go off to school, to learn to take orders (令).
齢.readings: レイ / よわい・とし
